title: ICC Revamps World Cup Formats: Super 7 Stage for ODIs, Super 10 and Eliminators for T20s
excerpt: The new structures, approved at the ICC Board's Edinburgh meetings, promise more high-stakes matches and blockbuster rematches — a windfall for Indian cricket fans worldwide.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • ICC introduces new formats for ODI and T20 World Cups to enhance competition.
  • ODI World Cup features a Super 7 stage, increasing match stakes and potential rematches.
  • T20 World Cup shifts to a Super 10 format, with direct semi-final qualifications for group winners.
  • 57 matches planned for the 2027 ODI World Cup, nine more than previous formats.
  • Changes promise more high-stakes matches for Indian cricket fans globally.
The International Cricket Council has approved sweeping changes to the formats of both the men's ODI World Cup and the men's T20 World Cup, introducing more rounds and higher-stakes progression systems designed to make every match count from day one. The decisions were announced following the ICC Board's annual meetings in Edinburgh, with the stated goal of "creating more meaningful contests, elevating competitive standards, and enhancing the tournament experience for athletes and fans," [the ICC said in its official release](https://www.icc-cricket.com/). ## ODI World Cup: Super 7 Replaces Super 6 The ODI World Cup will retain 14 participating teams — matching the 2015 edition's expanded field after the 2019 and 2023 editions featured only 10 — but will adopt a new four-round structure. A preliminary Super Series between the 12th, 13th, and 14th-ranked teams will open the tournament, with the winner advancing to Round 2 alongside the top 11 directly qualified teams. Round 2 will feature two groups of six. The top three from each group, plus the best fourth-placed team across both groups, will qualify for a Super 7 round-robin — a single league where all seven teams play each other, even if they met earlier in the tournament. "If India and Pakistan are placed in the same group in Round 2 and manage to qualify for the Super 7, they will clash again," [CricBuzz noted](https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/139552/icc-unveils-new-formats-for-mens-odi-and-t20-world-cups), highlighting the potential for blockbuster rematches. The top four from the Super 7 advance to the semi-finals (1 vs 4, 2 vs 3), followed by the final. The 2027 edition will feature 57 matches — nine more than the previous format. ## T20 World Cup: Super 10 and Eliminators The T20 World Cup will keep its 20-team field but undergo significant structural changes. The opening round will shift from four groups of five to five groups of four, with the top two from each group advancing.

The most notable change replaces the Super 8 stage with a Super 10 — two groups of five teams. Group winners will qualify directly for the semi-finals, while second-placed teams face third-placed teams from the opposite group in Eliminator matches, [borrowing a concept from the Indian Premier League](https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/139552/icc-unveils-new-formats-for-mens-odi-and-t20-world-cups). ## What It Means for India and the Diaspora For Indian cricket fans — both in India and across the global diaspora — the changes promise more high-stakes matches and a longer tournament window. The Super 7 format in ODIs guarantees that top teams face each other multiple times, increasing the chances of marquee India-Pakistan, India-Australia, and India-England clashes. Former India off-spinner Ravichandran Ashwin welcomed the changes on X, saying they would make global tournaments more competitive. However, he stressed that associate teams like the Netherlands, Nepal, and the United States need regular bilateral series — not just qualification tournaments — to genuinely develop, [The Impressive Times reported](https://www.impressivetimes.com/). The qualification structure for the 2028 T20 World Cup was also approved. Scotland received direct entry to the Europe Regional Final following the unusual circumstances surrounding their participation in the 2026 edition, where they replaced Bangladesh at the last hour. The format changes will undergo a final review by the ICC's Finance and Commercial Affairs Committee in November before formal ratification.
